data.title: Saudi Arabia Concludes Participation in 7th Worldwide Air Transport Conference in Montreal
data.content:
Montreal, November 21, 2026, SPA -- Saudi Arabia, represented by the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA), has concluded its participation in the 7th Worldwide Air Transport Conference (ATConf/7), organized by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) in Montreal, Canada, from November 16 to 20.
    Led by GACA President Abdulaziz Al-Duailej and comprising 44 representatives from 18 national entities, the delegation achieved key outcomes, including signing 12 agreements, memoranda of understanding, and records of discussion, submitting eight working papers, holding over 32 bilateral meetings, and hosting a special edition of the Future Aviation Forum.
    During the conference, Saudi Arabia signed bilateral air transport services agreements with Belize, Samoa, Cambodia, and Jordan; MoUs with Saint Lucia, Antigua and Barbuda, Montenegro, Cabo Verde, and Türkiye; and records of discussion with Macau, the Congo, and Equatorial Guinea to expand international cooperation and air connectivity. The delegation also presented eight working papers addressing economic regulation, sector resilience, investment, innovation, and sustainable growth, while participating in ICAO deliberations shaping the future of global air transport.
    Al-Duailej and the delegation held bilateral talks with ICAO Council President Toshiyuki Onuma, ICAO Secretary General Juan Carlos Salazar, Airports Council International (ACI) representatives, Bombardier, and 24 national delegations to explore sector development and exchange expertise. Additionally, in his capacity as Chair of the Executive Council of the Arab Civil Aviation Organization (ACAO), Al-Duailej presided over the eighth coordination meeting of regional civil aviation organizations to align positions ahead of upcoming assembly proceedings.
    On the sidelines of the event, Al-Duailej—who also chairs the Steering Committee of the Riyadh-based Regional Safety Oversight Organization for the Middle East and North Africa (MENA RSOO)—received the formal accession documents from Syria and Lebanon, bringing the organization's membership to 10 states.
    GACA also organized a special edition of the Future Aviation Forum in Montreal ahead of its next edition in Riyadh from April 19 to 21, 2027, further cementing the Kingdom's standing as a global aviation hub in line with Saudi Vision 2030.
    -- SPA
